Subject Gambling dens in the Western District - situation.
Made by D. S. I. Loh Wei Kong. Forwarded by D. S. I. Logan.

The following three small gambling
dens opened in the Western District, O.O.L.
on September 5 :-

Name Address Name of Conductor
Sung Kee Huh 43 Sing Kong Tsang Kuo Tseng

Huh Li (合利) 71 Zung Zoen Tsang Chi Ping
Company Li, Jessfield (張继口), loafer.
(previously Road.
unnamed)

Woo Ping (和平) First House,
Company Yien Tsuh Li,
Woo Ping Road,
off Bubbling
Well Road, O.O.L.

It will be remembered that the first
two mentioned gambling establishments were closed
on August 21, 1940, due to losses sustained. The
three dens pay a monthly fee of $6,000.00 each to
the East Asia Charity Association, Lane 1032, 25
Yu Yuen Road.

In addition, there are two leading gambling
dens operating in the Western District, namely the
"Loh Kuo Hotel", 346 Avenue Haig, and the "China Club",
29 Tifeng Road.

REPORT
Date Sept. 2, 19 40.

Subject Gambling raid in Pootoo Road District.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Logan

Acting on the authority of Shanghai Special
District Court Search Warrant, No.8 dated 1/9/40,
members of the Special Branch headed by D.S.I. Logan
in conjunction with a squad of 14 C.P.C.s and
F.S. MacFarlane from the Reserve Unit under Inspt.
Campbell, at 8.15 p.m. September 1, raided premises
No.4, Lane 234, Mapai Road, where public gambling
was reported to be in progress:

At the time of the Police visit, it was
learned that public gambling, which commenced there
in the morning and ended at 4 p.m. that date, had
just been started at that address on September 1,
as the premises in question were still under the
process of being decorated. Seven employees of the
den, known as the Hoong Shing Company (鸿兴),
were subsequently learned to have left the address
about half an hour prior to the Police arrival and
informed the three painters who were then at work
that they would return shortly afterwards. The
painters upon being interrogated by Police were
unable to supply any useful information regarding
the conductors and other particulars of the den.

A thorough search of the premises was
made and the following gambling paraphernalia was
seized and brought to Pootoo Road Station :-

6 brass boxes for chips.
2 porcelain pots for shaking dices.
1 large black wood pot with 3 dices.

（左侧栏内容）
Commmr. of Police.
Sir:
Information.
R.W. Yorke
D. C. (Sp. Br.)
2/9.

报告
日期：1940年9月2日。

主题：普陀路地区赌博突击行动。

由特别股督察洛根（Logan）制作并呈报

依据1940年9月1日签发的上海特区法院第8号搜查令的授权，由特别股督察洛根（Logan）率领的特别股成员，会同坎贝尔（Campbell）巡官麾下后备队的14名中国警员（C.P.C.s）及麦法伦（MacFarlane）副巡佐（F.S.），于9月1日晚8时15分，对马派路（Mapai Road）234弄4号的处所进行了突击搜查，据报该处正在进行公开赌博活动：

在警方抵达时获悉，该处的公开赌博活动于当日上午开始，至下午4时结束；鉴于相关处所当时仍在装修过程中，9月1日的赌博活动才刚刚开始。后得知，该赌窟（名为“鸿兴公司”）的七名雇员在警方到达前约半小时已离开该地址，并告知当时正在作业的三名油漆工他们稍后即回。经警方讯问，油漆工无法提供关于该赌窟经营者及其他细节的任何有用信息。

对该处所进行了彻底搜查，查获以下赌博用具并带至普陀路捕房：

6个用于存放筹码的黄铜盒。
2个用于摇骰子的瓷罐。
1个装有3颗骰子的大黑木罐。

（左侧栏内容）
警务处处长。
先生：
情报。
R.W. 约克（Yorke）
特别股副督察
9月2日。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 13 AUG 1940）

FILE
1/4

House 864 Yu Yuen Road was the former site
of the Broadway Club, a gambling den which opened
on December 23, 1939, with the approval of the
Japanese Amusement Supervision Office (now defunct).
It was closed on June 16, by order of the Japanese
Military Police but reopened on June 28 under the
title "New Asia Club". This den paid a "guarantee
Fund" of $100,000.00 and a further daily sum of
$3,333.00 to the Japanese Military Police for
permission to carry on their business. On July 31,
1940, the "New Asia Club" closed and amalgamated
with the "Loh Ku Hotel", a joint establishment
of six leading gambling dens which is located at
346 Avenue Haig.

Following the evacuation of the den, the
premises at 864 Yu Yuen Road were almost immediately
occupied as a temporary boarding house by some
ten members (usually armed with Mauser pistols)
under the command of one Van Ming (范敏) alias
Van Li Long (范利郎), a battalion commander
of the 'Peace and National Construction Army', who
is in charge of the liaison office for the Army in
question at 65 West End Gardens, Yu Yuen Road. Van
serves concurrently as a section chief of the Special
Service Group attached to the Shanghai Office of the
Ministry of Police, 76 Jessfield Road. Those ten

愚园路864号原为百老汇俱乐部（Broadway Club）旧址，这是一家赌博窝点，于1939年12月23日在日本娱乐监管所（现已撤销）的批准下开业。该窝点于6月16日奉日本宪兵队之令关闭，但于6月28日以“新亚俱乐部”之名重新开业。该窝点向日本宪兵队支付了100,000.00美元的“保证金”，并每日额外支付3,333.00美元，以获准继续经营。1940年7月31日，“新亚俱乐部”关闭，并与位于海格路346号的“罗古饭店”（Loh Ku Hotel）合并，后者是由六家主要赌博窝点联合经营的机构。

在该窝点撤离后，愚园路864号的 premises 几乎立即被大约十名成员（通常配备毛瑟手枪）占用，作为临时寄宿舍，其指挥官为范敏（Van Ming），别名范利郎（Van Li Long）。范敏系“和平建国军”营长，负责该部队在愚园路西区花园65号的联络处事务。范敏同时兼任极司菲尔路76号警察部上海办事处附属特务组的科长。那十名

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 10 AUG. 1940）

FILE

On August 10, a fight occurred between members of the Special Service Group attached to the Shanghai Office of the Ministry of Police and employees of a small gambling den named the "Hwa Song Club" (華商總會), 10 Zung Teh Fang, Jessfield Road, O.O.L. The trouble arose over an attempt by the Special Service Group to extort money from the den.

The Hwa Song Club came into existence on August 10, with Sung Sze Zung (孫樹成) as conductor and he was assisted by three Formosans who acted as guards. Prior to the opening of the den, attempts were made by Tsang Kuo Tseng (張國震), in charge of a section of the Special Service Group at 22 Sing Loh Tseng, Singapore Road, O.O.L., to obtain a monthly fee of $300.00 from the den but the demand was ignored. On the morning of August 10, a member of the section visited the den on instruction from Tsang Kuo Tseng and after losing at the gaming tables demanded the re-payment of $50.00 which was rejected. The waiter whom he asked for the money was carrying a kettle of hot water and collided with this person who then attempted to assault the waiter. The three Formosan guards immediately appeared while a number of the Special Service Group also appeared at the same time

华商总会于8月10日开业，由孙树成（Sung Sze Zung）负责经营，另有三名台湾人担任保镖协助其工作。在赌窟开业之前，负责越界筑路区域新加坡路（Singapore Road）22号特务组某分部的张国震（Tsang Kuo Tseng）曾试图向该赌窟收取每月300.00元的规费，但该要求被无视。8月10日上午，该分部一名成员奉张国震之命前往赌窟，在赌桌上输钱后，要求退还50.00元，遭到拒绝。当他向一名端着热水壶的服务员索要钱款时，与该服务员发生碰撞，随后企图殴打该服务员。三名台湾保镖随即出现，同时也有数名特务组成员赶到现场

Made by................ Det. Inspector Tabrum. Forwarded by................................................................

Sir;
Concerning the newley established Loh Koh Club,
346 Avenue Haig, F.S. Vaughan-Neale confidentially
notified D.I. Tabrum that these premises are the
property of a relative of his named "Yang", who was
compelled to lease the premises to a gambling
syndicate at a rental of $4,000.00 a month under the
following circumstances:
'About July 25, 1940 a party of armed men
entered 346 Avenue Haig and abducted Mr. Yang. He
was taken to a house in the Western Area where he
was ordered to remove from and surrender his home to
a gambling syndicate who would pay to him the sum of
$4,000.00 a month as compensation and rent. Mr.
Yang, who was liberated about two hours after being
abducted, and had no option but to accept the
demands, removed from his home on the following day.'
No official report of this case has been made
to the S.

先生：
关于新近成立的位于海格路346号的六合俱乐部（Loh Koh Club），F.S. Vaughan-Neale 秘密通知探目 Tabrum，该处房产属于其一名姓“杨”的亲属所有。在以下情形下，杨某被迫将该处所租赁给一个赌博集团，月租金为4,000.00美元：
‘约在1940年7月25日，一伙武装人员进入海格路346号，绑架了杨先生。他被带至西区的一处房屋，并被勒令搬离，将其住宅移交给一个赌博集团，该集团将每月支付给他4,000.00美元作为补偿和租金。杨先生在被绑架约两小时后获释，别无选择，只能接受要求，并于次日搬离其住所。’
本案未向本局提交正式报告。

Det. Inspector Tabrum

Sir;

（批：I D C S B）
        On the morning of August 2, 1940 information
from an outside source was received to the effect
that on the night of July 31, 1940 about 30 to 40
armed men walked into 864 Yu Yuen Road, the Broadway
Gambling Den, as it was about to close as a
gambling establishment, and took possession of the
premises.
      . These armed men were said to be members of
the China Peace National Salvation Army, with
head office in Shanghai established at 65 West
End Gardens.
（批：II S.I.）
（批：12/8）
        This information was corroborated on the
morning of August 10, 1940 when representatives
of the Shanghai Office of Ministry of Police, 76
Jessfield Road, were being interviewed in
connection with a missing child.
（批：□□□）
        The representative interviewed, in the course
of general conversation stated; that on the night
of the 7/8 August 1940 members of the Ministry of
Police were despatched to 864 Yu Yuen Road and
these members dispossessed the occupants, who left
when informed that instructions to dispossess them
of the premises had been issued by Lee Su Chuen,
Vice-Minister of Ministry of Police.

                                        1940年8月10日。
西区赌博 - 愚园路864号处所。
探目 Tabrum

先生：

（批注：I D C S B）
        1940年8月2日上午，收到来自外部渠道的情报，称1940年7月31日晚，约30至40名武装人员走进愚园路864号，即百老汇赌场（Broadway Gambling Den），当时该赌场正准备停止作为赌博场所营业，这些武装人员随即占据了该处所。
      . 据称，这些武装人员是“中国和平救国军”的成员，该组织在上海设有总部，地址为西园花园65号（65 West End Gardens）。
（批注：II S.I.）
（批注：12/8）
        1940年8月10日上午，这一情报得到证实，当时杰斯菲尔德路76号警察部上海办事处的代表因一起儿童失踪案正在接受问询。
（批注：□□□）
        受访代表在一般性谈话过程中陈述：1940年8月7日至8日晚，警察部成员被派往愚园路864号，这些成员驱逐了占据者；占据者在得知警察部副部长李士群已发出驱逐他们离开该处所的指令后离去。

page_data.en:
-Sheet 2-


The premises which are now being guarded by
four members of the Shanghai City Government Police
are being returned to their former owners, the
gambling den promoters.

The informant added that in view of the
numerous complaints received concerning the criminal
activities of the China Peace National Salvation
Army, there was every likelihood of Lee Sz Chuen
upon his return to Shanghai, issuing an order to
close up the office of this organization at 65
West End Gardens.


Kors.                                R. T. Joburn
                                     Det. Inspector


D.D.O. "B" Div.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS

JUL 28 1940

The Badlands:
New Gambling Den to Open
To the Editor of the
“NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS”
SIR,—It is quite some time now since we were promised that all gambling establishments on the outside roads were to be closed for good and yet nothing had been done up to the moment.
We know that practically all criminal acts emanate from these houses of chance (excepting, of course, political murders) and yet a new one situate at Yu Yuen Road, Lane 1032 House No. 25 is about to throw open its doors.
There is something doing at the moment amongst the foreign consuls of this city and all seem anxious to rid the settlement of further crime. and hope this letter will catch the eye of one who has the authority to stop issuing that necessary permit thus preventing the said gambling joint from opening up for business.
ACTION
Shanghai, July 27.

24th. July 40.

Information - Gambling in Western District.

Det. Inspector Tabrum
Officer i/c.

Sir;

With reference to remarks of Mr. H.D.F. Robertson,
A.C.C. (Services), on Afternoon Translation dated July
16, relevant to an article appearing in the Chinese
Press regarding the closure of gambling dens in the
Western area. I beg to report that according to
information from fairly reliable sources, there is an
indication that all the gambling dens in the Western
area, with the exception of the China Club, 25 Tifeng
Road, will cease functioning at 12 midnight on the
July 31, 1940.

However, prevalent among the gambling promoters,
to whom the order was given to close, is a rumour that
they will be permitted to re-open early in August 1940
and continue operations until midnight on the day
previous to the establishment of the Special Police
Force in the outside roads area.

R. E. Tabrum
Det. Inspector

There is no truth in the article appearing
in the July 16th issue of the Chinese-American Daily
News wherein they state that an order has been issued
by the Shanghai City Government for the closure of
all gambling dens in the Western District, O.O.L.
within three days.

The report appears to be a reproduction
of an article on the same subject which was published
on July 13 in the Central Daily News (Wang Ching Wei's
mouthpiece), but a correction, appeared in the same
paper the following day, July 14, stating that the
report was not true. (Translation attached).

There are seven leading gambling dens and
four small gaming establishments operating in the
Western District, O.O.L. The leading dens are
operating with permission from the Japanese Military
Police authorities, while the small dens have the
consent of the Western District Police Bureau.

July 16, 1940. Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News, Ta Mei Pao and National Herald :-

ALL GAMBLING DENS IN WESTERN DISTRICT TO BE CLOSED WITHIN
THREE DAYS.

It is reported that an order was issued
by the puppet City Government yesterday instructing all the
gambling dens in the Western District to close within three
days. It is stated that the object of this order is to
show its determination to do away with the gambling evil in
the controlled area.

It is observed that recently the puppet
City Government issued a similar order for the closure of the
gambling dens in the Western District, but the 10 big
gambling dens in the Western District reopened under changed
names after remaining closed for a time. The reopening of
these gambling dens was said to be due to a desire to relieve
the more than 100,000 persons who would have been thrown out
of employment through the closure of these dens.

It is learned that the Western District
Amusement Resorts Rehabilitation Association recently made
an appeal to the puppet Police Bureau of the City Government
for a longer period of operations by gambling dens in the
Western District, but this was turned down by the Police
Bureau.

1940年7月16日。下午译文。

《中美日报》、《大美晚报》及《国民新闻》：-

西区所有赌窟将在三天内关闭。

据报道，傀儡市政府昨日发布命令，指示西区所有赌窟在三天内关闭。据悉，此命令的目的是表明其消除控制区内赌博恶习的决心。

观察到近期傀儡市政府曾发布类似命令关闭西区赌窟，但西区的10家大型赌窟在关闭一段时间后，以更改名称的方式重新开业。据说这些赌窟的重新开业是为了缓解因赌窟关闭而失业的10多万人的困境。

获悉，西区游乐场所复兴协会最近向傀儡市政府警察局申请延长西区赌窟的运营期限，但被警察局拒绝。

July 13, 1940.

Central China Daily News :-

AMUSEMENT RESORTS IN WESTERN DISTRICT TO BE CLOSED WITHIN
THREE DAYS

During the most prosperous period of their
business 24 amusement resorts were in existence in the Western
District. They paid a total of $300,000 monthly to pay the
expenses of the Fire Brigade, the Benevolent Organization, the
Refugees' Hospital, etc. After the return of the National
Government to Nanking, these amusement resorts were once closed
by order of the local authorities. A Rehabilitation Committee
of Employees of Amusement Resorts in the Western District was
organized and made an appeal to the City Government to grant a
postponement of the order for six months so as to enable all
the employees to maintain their livelihood. At the same time,
the amusement resorts were reduced to 10 in all. They agreed
to pay the same monthly tax as before when 24 amusement resorts
were in existence. In addition to this tax, they are also
willing to pay a certain amount to cover the expenses for the
establishment of ten primary schools, two middle schools and
a public hospital.
As the matter was one which would greatly affect
the administration of the City Government, the appeal submitted
by the Committee was transmitted by the Shanghai City Government
to the Executive Yuan for record; at the same time it issued an
order to the Police Bureau of the City Government to close all
amusement resorts in the Western District within three days of
the date of the order.

July 14, 1940.

Central China Daily News :-

REPORT THAT AMUSEMENT RESORTS IN WESTERN DISTRICT
WILL BE CLOSED WITHIN THREE DAYS NOT TRUE

According to yesterday's newspapers, the
amusement resorts in the Western District were ordered by
the Police Bureau of the City Government to be closed within
three days. A petition was forwarded to the Ministry of
Police by the Rehabilitation Committee of Employees of
Amusement Resorts in the Western District requesting the
Ministry to grant a postponement of the order for six months
so as to enable all the employees to have a chance to find
other jobs. The request was not accepted by the Ministry
of Police. The report of the closure of the amusement
resorts within three days is, however, found to be untrue.
page_data.zh:
1940年7月13日。

《华中日报》：-

西区游乐场所将在三天内关闭

在业务最繁荣时期，西区曾有24家游乐场所。它们每月共支付30万元，用于支付消防队、慈善组织、难民医院等的费用。国民政府还都南京后，这些地方当局曾下令关闭这些游乐场所。随后成立了西区游乐场所员工复兴委员会，并向市政府申请将命令推迟六个月执行，以便所有员工维持生计。同时，游乐场所减少到总共10家。他们同意支付与24家游乐场所存在时相同的月度税款。除了这笔税款外，他们还愿意支付一定金额，用于建立十所小学、两所中学和一所公立医院的费用。
由于此事将极大影响市政府的行政管理，委员会提交的申请由上海市政府转呈行政院备案；同时，市政府向市警察局发出命令，要求在命令发布之日起三天内关闭西区所有游乐场所。

1940年7月14日。

《华中日报》：-

关于西区游乐场所将在三天内关闭的报道不实

据昨日报纸报道，市警察局命令西区游乐场所在三天内关闭。西区游乐场所员工复兴委员会向警政部递交请愿书，请求警政部将命令推迟六个月执行，以便所有员工有机会寻找其他工作。警政部未接受该请求。然而，经查证，关于游乐场所在三天内关闭的报道并不属实。

On July 13, CHU ZUNG LING (朱順林),
Manager of the "1238 Club," 1238 Yu Yuen Road,
took charge of the "East Asia Charity Relief
Association," Lane 126, A-23 Kinnear Road, in the
place of PAN SAN SING (潘三省).
This change was caused by dissension between
the two persons concerned. At the beginning of
July, PAN effected reorganization of the Amusement
Readjustment Committee and renamed the "East Asia
Charity Relief Association," under the pretext of
relieving the "unemployed" guards of the defunct
gambling dens. Actually he had the intention of
causing embarrassment to those dens which were
permitted to reopen by the Japanese Military Police.
On July 6, six gambling dens operating in the
Western District were ordered to close by the "East
Asia Charity Relief Association" in the name of the
Japanese Military Police, because of their refusal
to pay half of the net income which PAN SAN SING
demanded for so-called benevolent purposes. This
action on the part of PAN SAN SING incurred strong
opposition from the conductors of the six gambling
dens concerned who appealed to the Japanese
authorities for the suppression of the Association
in question. Mediation was conducted by LI SHIH CHUN
(李士群), Vice Minister of Police of the New
Central Government, and the gambling dens resumed
business on July 9.

7月13日，愚园路1238号“1238俱乐部”经理朱顺林（CHU ZUNG LING），接替潘三省（PAN SAN SING），接管了位于金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）A-23弄126号的“东亚慈善救济协会”。
此次变动系因上述两人之间发生分歧所致。7月初，潘三省以救济已关闭赌场的“失业”保镖为名，改组了娱乐业调整委员会，并将其更名为“东亚慈善救济协会”。实际上，他意在给那些获日本宪兵队许可重新开业的赌场制造麻烦。7月6日，“东亚慈善救济协会”以日本宪兵队的名义，命令西区六家赌场停业，原因是这些赌场拒绝向潘三省缴纳其以所谓慈善为目的所要求的半数净收入。潘三省的这一举动遭到了相关六家赌场经营者的强烈反对，他们向日本当局申诉，要求取缔该协会。经新中央政府警察部副部长李士群（LI SHIH CHUN）调解，这些赌场于7月9日恢复营业。

Western District Branch of the Japanese Military
Police failed to obtain a satisfactory explanation,
but believe that the officers in charge of the
Japanese Military Police are annoyed at the reopening
of these six dens within such a short period.
According an opinion expressed by the conductors,
only three of the dens should have opened first, the
remainder to resume business gradually.
        The conductors of the gambling dens concerned
are convinced that their closure was instigated by
PAN SAN SING of the "East Asia Charity Relief
Association" to cause embarrassment. They are of the
opinion that PAN has the intention of bringing pressure
to bear upon them so that he will be in a position
to obtain half of the net income of the dens for the
treasury of the "East Asia Charity Relief Association".
The conductors have so far refused to yield to this
proposal and are reported to have appealed to the
Japanese authorities for the suppression of the
"East Asia Charity Relief Association". LI SHIH CHUN
(李士群), Vice Minister of Police of the New Central
Government, is reported to be mediating in the dispute.

(签名)

日本宪兵队西区支队的查询未能获得令人满意的解释，但认为日本宪兵队负责人对在如此短的时间内重新开放这六家赌场感到恼火。根据经营者表达的意见，应该先开设其中三家赌场，其余的逐步恢复营业。
        相关赌场的经营者确信，他们的停业是由“东亚慈善救济协会”的潘三省煽动，旨在制造麻烦。他们认为，潘三省意图向他们施加压力，以便使其能够将赌场净收入的一半纳入“东亚慈善救济协会”的金库。迄今为止，经营者拒绝屈服于这一提议，并据报已向日本当局申诉，要求取缔“东亚慈善救济协会”。据报，新中央政府警察部副部长李士群（LI SHIH CHUN）正在调解此纠纷。

The Amusement Readjustment Committee, Lane 126,
A.23 Kinnear Road, has been renamed the "East Asia
Charity Relief Association" (東亞慈善救濟會) and
Pan San Sing (潘三省) will still be in charge.
He is reported to have obtained the support of the
Japanese Special Service Section through Yamaki (山本),
Japanese advisor to the Amusement Readjustment Committee
for the reorganization under the pretext of relieving
the hardships of the "unemployed" guards of the defunct
gambling dens. By forming the so-called "East Asia
Charity Relief Association", Pan has the intention of
causing embarrassment to those dens, especially the
"1238 Club", which have been permitted to reopen by the
Japanese Military Police Authorities.
On July 2, a party of six persons visited the
"1238 Club", formerly the Li Wei Lo Amusement Club,
1238 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L., and remained on the premises.
They claimed to have been despatched by the "East Asia
Charity Relief Association" with a view to supervising
the business of the club, and stated that similar parties
had been sent to the other dens which opened for business
recently. They further stated that half of the net
income of those gambling dens had to be turned over to
the treasury of the "East Asia Charity Relief Association"
for "benevolent" purposes. This action on the part of
the association embarrassed the conductors of the gambling
dens concerned to a considerable extent, and it is

According to information obtained, the following three gambling dens in the Western District, O.O.L., which closed on June 16, 1940, will reopen under new titles :-

(1) Li Wei Lo (利滙廬) Amusement Club. Behind Hollywood Garden, 1204 Yu Yuen Rd. O.O.L.

Made by D.S.I. Loh Wei-kong, Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

The conductors of the gambling dens now

CHINA PRESS
JUN 1940

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

Finance Investigation
THE Japanese call it the "Finance Investigation Society." And the name is quite appropriate. They investigate your finances and then take them away from you.
Upon entering the establishment, you are greeted by a Japanese civilian who escorts you into a large room and then the investigating business begins—over a roulette wheel.
The place is located at 82 Yates Road in the heart of the International Settlement. When the establishment was first opened several months, it was called the Sino-Japanese Research Association. The name was changed several weeks ago.
Just how this concern happens to be operating in the Settlement is one of the numerous official secrets they have hereabouts. I understand that because the place has official Japanese backing, the S.M.C. is a bit hesitant about taking direct action to close it up. However, the street fronting the premises of the "Finance Investigation Society" presents a rather interesting spectacle every evening. Police riot vans draw up to the curb and patrolmen and special search parties halt all and sundry.

Bad For Business
As a result of this intense activity in front of No. 82 Yates Road, very little "financial investigation" has taken place on the premises of that establishment for some time. The operators have complained more than once to the police that their search parties are "bad for our business." The police answer to that is that they are acting in interests of law and order. They can't afford to have any shootings around the Yates Road zone. Hence, the search party work continues in that area as a matter of routine.
A considerable flare-up developed Wednesday evening of last week, or maybe it was Thursday, when a Japanese member of the S.M.P. strolled into the picture and sought to remonstrate with members of the search party on behalf of the "Finance Investigation Society." As I get the story, he had no authority to interfere, but that didn't stop him. The argument became heated and the Japanese struck a foreign sergeant. I am told that the sergeant retaliated and that the search party work continued. It is still being carried on.

Commr. of Police.
Sir:
Information.
R. D. Lark
D. C. (Sp. Br.)

1/6

《字林西报》 (CHINA PRESS)
1940年6月

卡罗尔·D·奥尔科特 (CARROLL D. ALCOTT) 著：《我常常在想》

财务调查
日本人称之为“财务调查社”。这个名字相当贴切。他们调查你的财务状况，然后将其夺走。
进入该机构后，你会受到一名日本平民的迎接，他将你护送至一个大房间，随后“调查”业务便开始了——是在轮盘赌桌旁进行的。
该场所位于国际租界中心的耶茨路 (Yates Road) 82 号。几个月前该机构刚开业时，名为“中日研究会”。几周前更改了名称。
这家机构究竟为何能在租界内运营，是此地众多的官方秘密之一。我了解到，由于该场所有日本官方背景，工部局 (S.M.C.) 对采取直接行动予以关闭有些犹豫。然而，每晚在“财务调查社” premises 前的街道上都会呈现一番相当有趣的景象。警察防暴车停靠在路边，巡捕和特别搜查队拦截所有路人。

不利于生意
由于耶茨路82号门前这种高强度的活动，一段时间以来，该机构内几乎未进行什么“财务调查”。经营者已不止一次向警方抱怨，他们的搜查队“对我们的生意不利”。警方对此的回答是，他们是为了维护法律和秩序而行动。他们不能容忍耶茨路区域发生任何枪击事件。因此，该地区的搜查队工作作为例行公事继续进行。
上周三晚上，或者也许是周四，发生了一场相当大的冲突，当时一名上海公共租界工部局警务处 (S.M.P.) 的日本成员介入现场，试图代表“财务调查社”与搜查队成员交涉。据我所知，他无权干涉，但这并未阻止他。争论变得激烈，这名日本人殴打了一名外籍巡长。据说该巡长进行了还击，搜查队的工作继续进行。目前这项工作仍在持续。

警务总监。
先生：
情报。
R. D. Lark

Made by. D.S.I. Loh Wei Kong Forwarded by. D.I. Crawford

On May 31, a decision was reached and passed
by the Amusement Readjustment Committee, Lane 126,
20 Kinnear Road to close the following gambling dens:

(1) Soong Yuen (松園) 626 Avenue Haig, O.O.L.
(2) Yih Lo (怡) 368 Avenue Haig, O.O.L.
(3) Hillman Club 121 Yoong Yuan Pang,
(formerly known as Lane 1921, off
Yoong Yuan Amusement Bubbling Well Road,
Society) O.O.L.
(4) Li Wei Lo Amusement Behind Hollywood Garden,
Club 1204 Yu Yuen Road,
O.O.L.
(5) Honeymoon Club Premises next to 42
Great Western Road,
O.O.L.

The Honeymoon Club and the Soong Yuen
accordingly closed at 12 noon and 12 midnight of
May 31. The Li Wei Lo Amusement Club, however,
refused to obey the order, while the two others
have adopted a hesitating attitude and still
remain open.

The Li Wei Lo Amusement Club was closely
connected with the Amusement Readjustment Committee,
Lane 126, 20 Kinnear Road, then in charge of
LI SZE CHUNG (李士群). But on the departure of
LI SZE CHUNG for Nanking to assume the post of
Vice Minister of Police of the New Central Government,
PAN SAN SING (潘三省) took charge of the Amusement
Readjustment Committee, and he is said to be at
loggerheads with CHU ZUNG LING (朱順林), Manager
of the Li Wei Lo Amusement Club.

5月31日，位于金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）20号126弄的娱乐业调整委员会作出并通过了一项决定，关闭以下赌场：

(1) 松园（Soong Yuen），海格路（Avenue Haig）626号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.）。
(2) 怡庐（Yih Lo），海格路368号，越界筑路区。
(3) 希尔曼俱乐部（Hillman Club），涌泉坊（Yoong Yuan Pang）121号，
（前称静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）旁涌泉游艺社1921弄），越界筑路区。
(4) 利威罗游艺俱乐部（Li Wei Lo Amusement Club），好莱坞花园后方，
愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）1204号，
越界筑路区。
(5) 蜜月宫俱乐部（Honeymoon Club），大西路（Great Western Road）42号旁 premises，
越界筑路区。

据此，蜜月宫俱乐部和松园于5月31日中午12时和午夜12时关闭。然而，利威罗游艺俱乐部拒绝服从命令，另外两家则采取观望态度，仍然营业。

利威罗游艺俱乐部与位于金尼尔路20号126弄、当时由李士群（LI SZE CHUNG）负责的娱乐业调整委员会关系密切。但随着李士群前往南京就任新中央政府警政部副部长之职，潘三省（PAN SAN SING）接管了娱乐业调整委员会，据说他与利威罗游艺俱乐部经理朱顺林（CHU ZUNG LING）不和。

Following the receipt of an order for its
suspension, CHU ZUNG LING, Manager of the Li Wei Lo
Amusement Club, raised an objection and continued
functioning. All the guards in the employ of the
Club and followers of CHU ZUNG LING were assembled
on the premises and armed with some 100 Mauser
pistols with a view to taking precautions against
possible interference by the Amusement Readjustment
Committee. The manager was of the opinion that the
closure of the Li Wei Lo Amusement Club would affect
the livelihood of a large number of persons who
would interfere with peace and order if thrown out
of employment. This action on the part of the
manager of the Li Wei Lo Amusement Club has caused
considerable embarrassment to the Amusement
Readjustment Committee and the refusal to close by
this Club may affect the prestige of the Committee
and cause other gambling dens to follow its example.

A meeting was held later in the home of
PAN SAN SING, Lane 126, House 10 Kinnear Road,
which was attended by G. AKINO (秋野一馬),
known as Li Tsiu Ya (李秋野), an influential
Korean in the Western District connected with the
Japanese Special Service Section, one ITO (伊藤),
Chief of the Military Police in the Western District,
WOO SZE PAO (吳士寶), Chief of the Special Service
Group of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and

在收到停业令后，利威罗游艺俱乐部经理朱顺林提出抗议并继续营业。该俱乐部雇佣的所有警卫以及朱顺林的追随者都聚集在场所内，并配备了约100支毛瑟手枪，以防范娱乐业调整委员会可能的干预。该经理认为，关闭利威罗游艺俱乐部将影响大量人员的生计，这些人若失业将会扰乱治安秩序。利威罗游艺俱乐部经理的这一举动给娱乐业调整委员会造成了相当大的尴尬，而该俱乐部拒绝关闭可能会损害委员会的威信，并导致其他赌场效仿。

随后在潘三省家中举行了一次会议，地点位于金尼尔路10号126弄，出席者有秋野一马（G. AKINO），又名李秋野（Li Tsiu Ya），他是西区一位与日本特务机关有联系的有影响力的朝鲜人；伊藤（ITO），西区宪兵队队长；吴士宝（WOO SZE PAO），中国国民党反共救国军（地址：极司菲尔路76号）特务组组长；以及

Subject... Gambling Den in Western District - reported closure

Made by... D.S.I. Loh Wei Kong Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The news article appearing in the Chinese press of May 30th Issue in connection with the closure of the Hollywood gambling den, known as the Li Wei Lo (利派) Amusement Club, 1204 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L., is incorrect. The management of the gambling den deny having received any such instructions from the Japanese authorities and the den is still functioning to-day, May 30.

It is reported that a meeting is to be held in the Amusement Readjustment Committee, Lane 126, 20 Kinnear Road, in the afternoon of May 30 when the conductors of the gambling dens now operating in the Western District, O.O.L. will be in attendance to discuss the questions of their establishments and their closure. The majority of the conductors firmly believe that they will be ordered by the Amusement Readjustment Committee to close their dens on May 31 or at the beginning of June.

An unconfirmed report is to the effect that the premises of the Li Wei Lo, 1204 Yu Yuen Road, O.O.L. will be used as the "Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters."

5月30日中文版报纸上刊登的关于关闭被称为“利派”（Li Wei Lo）娱乐俱乐部的好莱坞赌场的新闻文章是不正确的。该赌场管理层否认收到日本当局的此类指令，且该赌场至今日（5月30日）仍在运营。

据报道，5月30日下午将在金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）20号126弄的“娱乐调整委员会”举行会议，目前在越界筑路区（O.O.L.）西区运营的赌场经营者将出席，讨论其场所的经营及关闭问题。大多数经营者坚信，他们将被娱乐调整委员会命令于5月31日或6月初关闭其赌场。

有一则未经证实的消息称，位于越界筑路区愚园路1204号的“利派”场所将被用作“吴淞上海警备司令总部”。

May 30, 1940. Morning Translation.

According to information from another source,
the gambling dens will resume operations after a certain
period because their employees, numbering more than 10,000,
will find it difficult to maintain their livelihood after
the closure. Therefore, the reduction of dens will be made
gradually. Whether this information is true or not remains
to be seen.
The Hollywood Gambling Den on Yu Yuen Road was
forced to close down yesterday by the Japanese authorities.
It is learned that upon its closure the gambling den will
undergo repairs and all its paraphernalia will be removed.
It is reported that the new government will establish on
the premises a so-called "Woosung-Shanghai Garrison
Commissioner's Headquarters." According to information from
another source, the premises will be used as the headquarters
of the Special Police Force.

National Herald, Ta Mei Pao and Chinese-American Daily News :-

BRITISH SOLDIER ATTEMPTS TO CUT DOWN FLAGPOLE OF GERMAN BANK

According to an announcement made to-day, on the
afternoon of May 26 a British soldier suddenly broke into
the Deutsch-Asiatische Bank, a German bank, on Kiukiang Road,
with the intention of cutting down the German flagpole on
the roof of the bank with a saw and at the same time he
destroyed several (    ) window panes. He was taken to a
Police Station by a police constable. In this connection,
the German Consul-General at Shanghai lodged a protest with
the S.M.C. yesterday and demanded a satisfactory settlement
of the event.----Transocean.
Furthermore according to the Ta Chung News
Agency, the British soldier in question was taken to offer
an apology to the German Consul-General; hence the matter
will probably be settled.

National Herald and Chinese-American Daily News :-

BRITISH SOLDIERS' FAMILIES REMOVE FROM BADLANDS

Several families of the British Defence Force
at Shanghai removed from the Chung Yih Hsin Tsung (中一新村)
lane on Edinburgh Road and Kinnear Road, Western District,
yesterday morning. The reason for their removal is the
poor sanitation in the Badlands.

据另一来源消息，赌场将在一段时间后恢复运营，因为其员工人数超过10,000人，关闭后难以维持生计。因此，赌场的减少将是逐步进行的。此消息是否属实，尚待观察。
位于愚园路的好莱坞赌场昨日被日本当局强制关闭。据悉，关闭后该赌场将进行修缮，所有设备将被移除。据报道，新政府将在该处设立所谓的“吴淞上海警备司令总部”。据另一来源消息，该处所将被用作特种警察部队总部。

《国民日报》、《大美报》和《中美日报》：

英军士兵试图砍倒德国银行旗杆

据今日宣布，5月26日下午，一名英国士兵突然闯入位于九江路的德国银行——德华银行（Deutsch-Asiatische Bank），意图用锯子砍倒银行屋顶上的德国旗杆，同时他打碎了几块（    ）窗玻璃。他被一名巡捕带往警局。就此事件，德国驻上海总领事昨日向工部局提出抗议，并要求对此事作出令人满意的解决。----德意志通讯社。
此外，据大中通讯社报道，涉事英国士兵已被带去向德国总领事道歉；因此此事可能得以解决。

《国民日报》和《中美日报》：

英军家属搬离“坏地”

上海英国防卫队的几户家庭于昨日上午从西区爱丁堡路和金尼尔路上的中一新村（Chung Yih Hsin Tsung）弄堂搬出。他们搬迁的原因是“坏地”（Badlands）卫生条件恶劣。

Subject Hwo Wei Lottery in Western District

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Information has been received to the effect that a "hwo-wei" lottery was re-established on May 14 in the Western District. The headquarters have been given the name of "Yih Li" (益利) situated at 94 Yoong Yuen Pang, off Bubbling Well Road, O.C.L., and is in charge of WOO SZE PAO (吴安保), chief of the Special Service Group of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army, 76 Jessfield Road, with one LOH PAH LOH (陸伯樂), as his assistant. WOO SZE PAO is said to have agreed to pay $500.00 a day to the Amusement Readjustment Committee, Lane 126, No.20 Kinnear Road, for permission to conduct the lottery.

It will be remembered that "hwo-wei" lottery dens in the Western District, O.O.L. were closed on March 31, 1940 in accordance with instructions issued by the Amusement Readjustment Committee. A number of them, however, resumed functioning in April with approval unofficially from certain prominent members of the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army.

Following the formal opening of this headquarters for a "hwo-wei" lottery, the dens which were closed are now making arrangements with WOO SZE PAO for re-starting.

C. Crawford

The "Amusement Readjustment Committee" which was formed on March 31, 1940, at No.20, Lane 126, Kinnear Road, under the joint auspices of the Japanese Military Police and the Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern & National Salvation Army to control the gambling dens in the Western District, has decided to increase the protection fee levied from the gambling establishments, in accordance with the following scale with effect from to-day, April 11, 1940:-

| Amount of protection fee prior to April 11, 1940 | Amount of protection fee with effect from April 11, 1940 |
| :--- | :--- |
| Small gambling dens $150.00 each per diem | $600.00 each per diem |
| Large gambling dens $200.00 to $700.00 each per diem. | $1,000.00 each per diem |

The above decision to increase the protection fee, the Amusement Readjustment Committee announced, was passed as a result of observation of the business of the establishments during the past ten days. According to the organ, the business of the gambling dens now in existence in the Western District has increased two to three times that prior to the 31st of March, when eleven establishments were closed in accordance with a reorganization scheme of the organ.

Liao Chung Chien

Date 2nd.. April 1940.
Subject Information - Gambling establishments Western Area.
Made by Det. Inspector Tabrum Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir;
Information has been received from a reliable source to the effect that a gambling den, to be known as the "China Club", with premises at 29 Tifeng Road, formerly occupied by the Shanghai Middle School, is to be opened on the evening of 2-4-40.
The premises 29 Tifeng Road is a spacious three story foreign style house, and is immediately opposite the residence of Sir Elly Kadoorie.
Zia Pao Sung (謝葆生), the present owner of Ciro's Cabaret, 444 Bubbling Well Road, is said to have been appointed manager by Pan San Shing (潘三省), who, since the closing of the Shanghai Amusement Protection Agency Office (a Japanese organization), 470/9 Yu Yuen Road, has been elected as "Chief Representative" of all gambling establishments in the Western Area.
Pan San Shing, it should be noted here, was placed in office by Lee S Chung (李自群) of 76 Jessfield Road.
Nine of the smaller gambling houses have been compelled to close because they are unable to pay the monthly protection fee demanded of them by Pan San Shing's agency.
The Shanghai City Government Police Bureau, acting on the orders of the Japanese Military Police, have closed all Hwo Wei establishments in the Western Area as from 31-3-40.

[Signature]
Det. Inspector
D.D.O. "B" Div.

During the past fortnight contradictory
reports regarding the fate of the gambling dens in
the Western District, O.O.L., have appeared in the
local press. Some reports have stated that the
gambling dens have suspended operations or are about
to close while others contain flat denials of such
information.

Although no exact information regarding
the situation of the gambling dens is available,
it is nevertheless believed that the reorganization
scheme as reported by this office on 13-2-40, will
be carried out. The gambling dens will, in
accordance with an agreement reached between the
Japanese Authorities and Wang Ching Wei, be placed
under the control of the New Central China Government
to be inaugurated on 30-3-40. There are at
present 24 gambling dens in the Western District,
and a number of the smaller establishments will be
closed either through forcible measures or through
increased taxes which it is the intention of the
Authorities to levy knowing that they will not be
able to pay. The larger establishments permitted
to remain open for business will be required to
furnish between them, a sum equivalent to the
protection fees that are paid by those small dens
which will be closed as a result of the reorganization

March 24,1940. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and Shun Pao :-

GAMBLING DENS IN WESTERN DISTRICT ORDERED TO CLOSE DOWN
ON MARCH 29

According to information from reliable
sources, the Japanese authorities have decided to order
the gambling dens in the Western District to close down on
March 29. Should any of the gambling dens fail to observe
the order, the Japanese authorities will follow the
procedure they have adopted in Nantao by sealing up the
establishments and arresting the gamblers and the conductors
and subjecting them to heavy punishments.
It is also learned that the Hollywood, the
Victoria and other big gambling dens have expressed their
willingness to close down their establishments voluntarily
and that they are seeking accommodation in Macao in order
to resume their activities.

西区赌博窝点奉命于3月29日关闭

据可靠消息来源称，日本当局已决定命令西区的赌博窝点于3月29日关闭。如有任何赌博窝点不遵守该命令，日本当局将效仿其在南市采取的做法，查封场所，逮捕赌徒和经营者，并予以严厉惩罚。

CHINA PRESS.

MAR 21 1940

Operators Deny Reported
Closure Of Gambling Dens

Operators of Shanghai's
notorious gambling dens yester-
day vehemently denied reports
circulated recently that their
establishments would be closed
before the month ends.
Interviewed by THE CHINA
PRESS, operators of three of
the largest houses almost with
one accord blamed opposition
groups for spreading the
"rumors."
"We are not closing today, or
at any time in the future," one of
the operators said. "Business is
good, flourishing, and our customers
are satisfied."
Asked regarding the motive of
the alleged rumors, the opera-
tor stated that "opposition
interests backed by enormous
financial resources have for a
long time been trying to dis-
lodge us from our positions. But
they won't succeed," he added
significantly.
The operator continued: "If you
don't believe we are staying open,
just come down and see." He also
revealed that with his establish-
ment he was taking no chances.
"The place is duly guarded," he
said.
Although scheduled to close up
on March 10, according to reports,
the gambling dens were given a
new lease on life on payment of
$20,000 each to responsible authori-
ties for further protection. The
reports had it that the new lease
would be valid until March 31.
In addition to the payment of a
flat fee for the "concession" to the
puppet city regime and to Japan-
ese quarters, each gambling den also
pays a monthly "protection fee."
The money paid on March 10, it
was stated, was an extraordinary
fee, necessitated by increasing
pressure exercised by the "opposi-
tion interests."

《字林西报》。

1940年3月21日

经营者否认有关
赌博窝点关闭的报道

上海臭名昭著的赌博窝点的经营者昨日强烈否认最近流传的关于其场所将在月底前关闭的报道。
在接受《字林西报》采访时，三家最大场所的经营者几乎一致指责反对派散布这些“谣言”。
“我们今天不会关闭，将来任何时候也不会，”其中一名经营者说。“生意很好，很兴隆，我们的顾客也很满意。”
当被问及所谓谣言的动机时，该经营者表示，“拥有巨大财力支持的反对派利益集团长期以来一直试图将我们赶下台。但他们不会成功，”他意味深长地补充道。
该经营者继续说道：“如果你不相信我们会继续营业，就下来看看。”他还透露，他的场所采取了万全之策。“地方已妥善 guarded，”他说。
据报道，虽然原定於3月10日关闭，但赌博窝点通过向负责当局各支付20,000美元以获得进一步保护，从而获得了新的生机。据报道，新的许可有效期将持续至3月31日。
除了向傀儡市政政权和日本方面支付固定的“特许权”费用外，每个赌博窝点还需每月支付“保护费”。据说，3月10日支付的款项是一笔额外费用，这是由于“反对派利益集团”施加的压力日益增大所致。

（批：69/... 8/4/3 Page 1/3）

The Shanghai News (新上海报), a mosquito newspaper,
published on March 19, 1940, the following article
written by one Bo Wang (霸王) :-

THE CLOSURE OF THE WESTERN DISTRICT CLUBS.

The reports in the newspapers
regarding the closure of the clubs in the Western
District are absolutely untrue; this question of
closure is entirely outside the realm of the
agreement over the Outlying Roads. Though the
"Supervision Department" has been dissolved, another
new organization is established to take over the
management. The responsible person is one named Lee
(李). It is learned that measures for the suppression
of opium will be adopted, and that the clubs in the
Western District will be gradually suppressed within
two years.

Shun Pao :-

CLOSURE OF GAMBLING DENS IN THE BADLANDS

Owing to the prohibition by the Japanese
authorities, all the gambling dens in Nantao suspended
their business yesterday when Japanese gendarmes visited
the establishments and nailed wooden boards across their
doors.

The Japanese authorities have also withdrawn
the licences of the gambling dens located in the Western
District of Shanghai and have ordered them to close down
as from to-day. On this account, the Hollywood (好萊塢),
the Yoong Sung (榮生), the Autumn Garden (秋園), the Yu
Yuen (愚園), the Jessfield Home (兆豐), the Broadway
(百老匯) and other gambling dens have ceased operations.

CHINA PRESS
MAR 2 1940

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

Shanghai Silhouettes
THE presence of several policemen and a handful
of American Marines in front of 82 Yates Road
on Wednesday night had a dampening effect on the
scheduled opening of the "Asia Economic Research
Society." The new gaming establishment with its
big electric sign in numerals, "82," presented an in-
viting appearance to individuals willing to part with
their lucre in the name of "research," but nothing
happened. The police say they were on the spot just
to see that no "frightfulness" developed. But a lot
of people got the impression that the officers were
picketing the place.

Speaking of roulette wheels and such like,
Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips, Secretary and Com-
missioner-General of the Shanghai Municipal
Council, is reported to have told an interviewer
a few days ago that the S.M.C. is planning to
issue a statement on the Council's policy con-
cerning gambling in the International Settle-
ment. I understand that it will be a blanket
statement, covering all angles of gambling. This
is rather interesting news to a lot of people who
were beginning to doubt that the Council
actually had a policy on gambling.

卡罗尔·D·奥尔科特随笔：我常常在想

上海剪影
周三晚上，几名警察和一小队美国海军陆战队员出现在耶茨路82号门前，这对原定于当晚开幕的“亚洲经济研究会”起到了抑制作用。这家新的赌博场所挂着巨大的数字电招牌“82”，对那些愿意以“研究”名义挥霍钱财的人呈现出诱人的外观，但什么也没发生。警方称他们到场只是为了确保不发生“恐怖事件”。但许多人觉得警官们是在对该地点进行纠察。

说到轮盘赌之类的事情，据报道，上海工部局秘书兼总办 G. Godfrey Phillips 先生几天前在接受采访时透露，工部局计划就国际公共租界内的赌博政策发表声明。我了解到这将是一份涵盖赌博各个方面的全面声明。这对许多开始怀疑工部局是否真的有关于赌博的政策的人来说，是个相当有趣的新闻。

The two men were Lee Yung and Zung Sing Fangand

Zung Shiu Chung on being questioned stated he was

A number of persons were detained on these

After being dismissed Zung Shiu Chung decided to
help them to get away and accordingly went to the home
of Lee Yung's friend at 10 Tau Zung Li, Rt. Vallon and
arranged with him and Lee's wife to bring a hire car to
Yu Yuen Road and promised he would produce the two
prisoners.
He returned to his late place of employment and on
the pretext of wishing to clean the cells obtained the
keys from the Japanese Officer in charge and released
the two prisoners, who entered the car and were arrested

向走在北侧人行道上的两名男子大喊，这两名男子随即上了车。
这两名男子是李荣和陈标方，当他们上车时，那名女子下了车。就在此时，副督察布雷瑟顿赶到现场，将他们带往警局。
经讯问，陈淑祥陈述他在愚园路470/9号任职茶房，该处是娱乐管理局的一个办事处，但他于1940年5月20日上午被解雇（注：原文日期可能有误，结合上下文应为3月20日或之前）。
陈称，有许多人被拘禁在这些 premises（场所）内，其中两人请求他帮助他们逃跑。这两人就是李荣和陈标方。
被解雇后，陈淑祥决定帮助他们逃离，于是前往李荣朋友位于法租界华伦路大钟里10号的住所，与其及李的妻子安排了一辆出租车到愚园路，并承诺他会把两名囚犯带出来。
他回到之前的工作地点，借口想要打扫牢房，从负责的日本军官那里拿到钥匙，释放了两名囚犯，他们进入汽车后如上所述被捕。

page_data.en:
Misc.No. 214/40.
1/3.

Both the released men state they were arrested
some months ago in gambling houses and charges of
cheating and detained at 470/9 Yu Yuen Road ever since.
D.I. Tabrum and Inspector Yamaguchi visited 470/9
Yu Yuen Road but could find no one in authority on the
premises. The only Japanese there stated he was not
aware that the prisoners had escaped.
Lee and Zung had stated that two other persons
were detained on the premises but the S.M.P. Officers
could find no trace of them.
The particulars of the case were communicated to
Mr. T.Robertson, D.C.(Crime) by Supt. Conduit, D.D.O."B"
Div., who instructed that Zung Shiu Chung, Lee Yung and
Zung Sing Fang be detained pending a decision by
Headquarters as to their disposal, and the other two be
allowed to go.
Statements attached.

杂项编号. 214/40.
1/3.

两名被释放者均陈述他们数月前在赌场被捕，被控作弊，并一直被拘禁在愚园路470/9号。
塔布鲁姆督察（D.I. Tabrum）和山口督察（Inspector Yamaguchi）走访了愚园路470/9号，但在现场未找到任何负责人。在场的唯一一名日本人声称他不知道囚犯已经逃脱。
李和陈曾陈述还有另外两人被拘禁在该处，但工部局警务处官员未能找到他们的踪迹。
"B"区副主管康杜伊特巡官（Supt. Conduit）将此案详情通报给刑事科副总办 T.Robertson 先生，后者指示拘押陈淑祥、李荣和陈标方，等待总部决定如何处置，其余两人予以释放。

page_data.en:
Lee Yung (李榮)
Canton                                      Clerk Lee Hong Nyih.
B'Well Stn.             20-3-40.

My name is Lee Yung age 60, native of Canton, M/seek,
formerly residing at place of employment ? Yunnan Road.
At 2.30 p.m. 11-9-39, while I was gambling in the
Yung Yuen Gambling Den, Great Western Road, I was arrested
by 9 or 10 male Chinese who were armed with pistols for
cheating in gambling and later taken to No.9, Lane 470 Yu Yuen
Road, where I was beaten first and later removed to a cell
below the staircase as a prisoner.
I was given ten cakes per day as my food by them.
At 2 p.m. 20-3-40, I was told by a teaboy named Zung Shiu
Chung (許就群) that I now can be released. Zung Shiu Chung
told me to wait on Yu Yuen Road as a hire car will sent for
me. When I left the above place, I saw the hire car arrive, but
on attempting to board the car, a foreign Police Officer
approached and brought us to the B'Well Police Station.
The above is my true statement.
page_data.zh:
李荣 (李榮)
广东                                      书记员 Lee Hong Nyih.
贝威尔路警局             1940年3月20日.

我叫李荣，年龄60岁，广东籍，职业求职中，此前居住在就业地？云南路。
1939年9月11日下午2点30分，当我在大西路永园赌场赌博时，被9或10名持枪的中国男子以赌博作弊为由逮捕，随后被带到愚园路470弄9号，在那里我先遭到殴打，后来作为囚犯被关进楼梯下的牢房。
他们每天给我十个饼作为食物。
1940年3月20日下午2点，一名叫陈淑祥（许就群）的茶房告诉我，我现在可以被释放了。陈淑祥让我在愚园路等候，说会派一辆出租车来接我。当我离开上述地点时，我看到出租车到达，但当我试图上车时，一名外籍警官走近并将我们带到贝威尔路警局。
以上是我的真实供词。

page_data.en:
Zung Sing Fang (陳三成).
Canton                                      Clerk Lee Hong Nyih.
B'Well Stn.             20-3-40

My name is Zung Sih Fang, age 35, native of Canton,
M/brass-smith, formerly residing at 1250 Avenue Road.
At 11 a.m. 11-9-39, while I was gambling at Yung Yuen
Gambling Den, Great Western Road, I was suddenly arrested by
two Japanese in plain clothes, for cheating in gambling and
later taken to No.9, Lane 470 Yu Yuen Road, where I was badly
beaten and after removed to a cell, below the staircase.
I was given ten cakes per day by them for my food. I
cleaned the ordure buckets daily at 2 p.m. I was kept there
until 2p.m. 20-3-40, when I was told by a tea boy named Zung
Shiu Chung (陳少章) that I now can be released. The tea boy
told me to wait on Yu Yuen Road as one of my friends would send
a hire car for me. As I left the place I saw a car arrive with
my friend named Wong Ching Yoong inside the car, but on
attempting to board the car, a foreign Police Officer approached
and brought us to the station.
I had previously informed the tea boy that if he could
effect my arrest, I would reward him.
The above is my true statement.
page_data.zh:
陈三成 (陳三成).
广东                                      书记员 Lee Hong Nyih.
贝威尔路警局             1940年3月20日

我叫陈标方（注：此处中文名与英文拼音 Zung Sih Fang 对应，但中文写作陈三成，可能为笔误或别名），年龄35岁，广东籍，职业铜匠，此前居住在爱文义路1250号。
1939年9月11日上午11点，当我在大西路永园赌场赌博时，突然被两名便衣日本人以赌博作弊为由逮捕，随后被带到愚园路470弄9号，在那里我遭到毒打，之后被关进楼梯下的牢房。
他们每天给我十个饼作为食物。我每天下午2点清理粪桶。我一直被关在那里直到1940年3月20日下午2点，当时一名叫陈少章（注：此处中文名与上文陈淑祥不同，可能为同一人或笔误）的茶房告诉我，我现在可以被释放了。茶房让我在愚园路等候，说我的一个朋友会派出租车来接我。当我离开该地时，我看到一辆车到达，我的朋友王金永在车里，但当我试图上车时，一名外籍警官走近并将我们带到警局。
我之前曾告诉茶房，如果他能帮我获释，我会酬谢他。
以上是我的真实供词。

page_data.en:
Zung Shiu Chung (陈树章)
Tai-chow, Chekiang D.S.I. Chu Chi Huang
B'well Station 20th.March 1940

My name is Zung Shiu Chung, age 40, native of Taichow,
Chekiang, and I am employed by the Japanese Amusement Super-
vision Office situated at No.470/9 Yu Yuen Road as a tea-boy.
I entered the employ of the above mentioned office on
1-6-39, and receive a wage of $15.00 per month with free food
and lodging. Since I worked there I have seen many persons
detained and released by the Japanese for alleged violation
of amusement rules in the gambling houses.
In Sept. 1939, I saw another 2 male Chinese taken into
custody, they were Cantonese and were detained together with
some 10 persons previously arrested.
On 10-3-40, this office was disbanded and all Japanese
except one of them departed. The prisoners, however, were
still detained. I sent food to the prisoners every day and
when I went there yesterday(19-3-40) morning, one of the
Cantonese prisoners asked me if I could help him to escape.
He promised to invite me to a feast if I would do it. He then
told me that he had a friend named Wong Ching Yung residing
at No.10 Dan Sing Lee, Route Vallon, French Concession, and
asked me to go and see him regarding his release. I promised
him to consider the matter. I was given $100.00 by the
Japanese this morning(20-3-40) and was told that I was no
longer required there as the place is going to close down.
The money is for my "pay-off". Thinking that it will be a
good chance to release the Cantonese, I went to the Cantonese
friend's home on Route Vallon, F.C., at about 11 a.m. and
told him the news. The man then informed the prisoner's wife
page_data.zh:
陈树章 (陈树章)
浙江台州 副督察 Chu Chi Huang
贝威尔路警局 1940年3月20日

我叫陈淑祥，年龄40岁，浙江台州籍，受雇于位于愚园路470/9号的日本娱乐监督办公室，担任茶房。
我于1939年6月1日进入上述办公室工作，月薪15.00美元，包食宿。自从我在那里工作以来，我看到许多人因涉嫌违反赌场娱乐规则而被日本人拘留和释放。
1939年9月，我看到另外两名中国男子被拘留，他们是广东人，与此前逮捕的大约10人一起被关押。
1940年3月10日，该办公室解散，除一人外所有日本人均已离开。然而，囚犯仍被拘留。我每天给囚犯送食物，昨天（1940年3月19日）早上我去那里时，其中一名广东囚犯问我是否能帮他逃跑。他承诺如果我这样做就请我吃大餐。然后他告诉我，他有一个朋友叫王金永（注：此处拼音为 Wong Ching Yung，与前文 Wong Ching Yoong 略有差异），住在法租界华伦路丹辛里10号，让我去见他商量释放事宜。我答应考虑此事。今天早上（1940年3月20日）日本人给了我100.00美元，并告诉我因为地方要关闭，不再需要我了。这笔钱是我的“遣散费”。我想这是一个释放广东人的好机会，于是在上午11点左右去了法租界华伦路的那位广东朋友家，告诉了他这个消息。那人随后通知了囚犯的妻子

page_data.en:
-Sheet 2-

who is living on Avenue Road and we all proceeded to Yu Yuen
Road with a hire car. I told the car to stop outside lane
470, Yu Yuen Road, when I alighted and went into the lane to
get the prisoners. His friend and wife waited in the car. I
obtained a key from the Japanese who is still there on the
ground that I wanted to go inside the prison to clean up the
place. I succeeded in releasing the two Cantonese and took
them to the waiting motor car and all of us intended to
escape but were arrested by the foreign policeman who suspected
us of being criminals.
page_data.zh:
-第2页-

此人居住在爱文义路（Avenue Road），我们随即乘一辆出租车前往愚园路。我让车停在愚园路470弄口，随后下车进入弄堂去提犯人。他的朋友和妻子在车里等候。我从仍在那里的日本人那里拿到一把钥匙，借口要进监狱打扫卫生。我成功释放了两名广东人，将他们带到等候的汽车旁，我们本打算逃跑，但被一名怀疑我们是罪犯的外国警察逮捕。

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS.
MAR 15 1940

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S.B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 8039A/41 Date 20 3 40）

I'VE OFTEN WONDERED BY CARROLL D. ALCOTT

New Gambling Den
ALTHOUGH the news has not been generally nois-
ed about, Shanghai is scheduled to get a new
gambling den in the near future. This one is to be
located in the International Settlement and the place
will be 82 Yates Road.
The establishment is to be run by the same crowd
that controls the Asia Club on Gordon Road
and will be operated largely for Chinese only.
I understand that the promoters of the venture
have been assured that they will have the same
protection given to the Gordon Road establishment
and, as a result, are sinking considerable money in
the project.

Modus Vivendi
The prevailing tense situation in the
badlands reminds me that S. M. C. Chair-
man Cornell S. Franklin and "Hizzoner" Fu
Siao-en recently signed an agreement intended
to bring into existence a joint police force in-
tended to end all this "wild west" business in
Shanghai. It seems that all that remains to be
done is to decide on some modus vivendi for
the operation of this force. Just when this will
be achieved is a matter of considerable specu-
lation about the city at the moment. Some of
the lads in a position to know are giving odds
that it will not be before 1941.

（批：Ruty 19/3）

（印：INDEXED BY (S.B.) REGISTRY DATE 20/3/40）

《大美晚报》（CHINA PRESS）
1940年3月15日

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别分部登记处 编号 S. B. D. 8039A/41 日期 1940年3月20日）

卡罗尔·D·奥尔科特（Carroll D. Alcott）撰文：《我常常在想》

新赌场
尽管消息尚未广泛传开，但上海计划在不久的将来开设一家新赌场。该赌场将位于公共租界内，地址为叶茨路（Yates Road）82号。
该场所将由控制戈登路（Gordon Road）亚洲俱乐部的同一伙人经营，且主要仅面向中国人开放。
据我了解，该项目的发起人已得到保证，他们将获得与戈登路场所相同的保护，因此正在这项工程中投入大量资金。

临时共存模式
不良地带（badlands）目前的紧张局势让我想起，上海公共租界工部局主席康奈尔·S·富兰克林（Cornell S. Franklin）和“市长”傅筱庵最近签署了一项协议，旨在建立一支联合警察部队，以终结上海这种“狂野西部”式的混乱局面。看来，剩下的工作只是确定这支部队行动的某种临时共存模式（modus vivendi）。至于何时能实现这一点，目前在全市范围内引起了诸多猜测。一些知情人士甚至打赌，这在1941年之前是无法实现的。

（批注：Ruty 3月19日）

Shooting of Dau Zung Zien
(陶順泉) on B'Well Road. O. O. L.

At 1.10p.m. 14/3/40 a telephone message was received
from the manager of the New Royal Hotel, B'Well Road, to
the effect that a male Chinese had been shot by two others
outside the above premises.

C.D.C. 147 and D.S.I. Young together with S.I.s
Phillips and Dainty attended and learned that a male
Chinese had been shot by two others at the entrance of
the lane leading into Delight Villas, next to the New
Royal Hotel, and the body removed by the ambulance of
the S.C.G.P.B.

Enquiries by D.S.I.s Young and Yao, C.D.S. 283 and
C.D.C. 147 learned the injured man to be one Dau Zung
Zien (陶順泉) employed as an unarmed watchman at the
Hillman House Gambling Den, 1926 Bubbling Well Road and
residing 65 Yoong Yuen Pang (永源浜) Bubbling Well
Road.

On the morning of 14/3/40 he went to work at 6.30
a.m. as usual and at 12noon went home for tiffin. He
returned to his place of employment at about 1p.m. and
saw five men loitering in a suspicious manner inside
the Hillman House compound. He pointed them out to
the other watchmen and on seeing this the strangers ran

静安寺路陶順泉（Dau Zung Zien）枪击案。O. O. L.

1940年3月14日下午1时10分，接到静安寺路新皇家酒店（New Royal Hotel）经理的电话报告，称一名华籍男子在上述处所外被另外两人枪击。

中央巡捕房147号和副督察杨（Young）会同巡佐菲利普斯（Phillips）和丹蒂（Dainty）到场调查，获悉一名华籍男子在新皇家酒店旁通往德利别墅（Delight Villas）的弄堂入口处被另外两人枪击，伤者已由山东路中央捕房（S.C.G.P.B.）的救护车送走。

CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.D.8039A/41(C)
Section 1, Special Branch. XXXX,
REPORT
Date March 11, 1940.
Subject Gambling Dens in the Western District - permits issued by the
Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department withdrawn.
Made by....................................................Forwarded by....................................................

At 3 p.m., March 10, 1940, the various
gambling dens in the Western District received a
telephonic message from the Shanghai Amusement
Supervision Department, 9/470 Yu Yuen Road,
instructing them to hand over the permits, which
were issued to them by the department, to the
Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern & National Salvation Army, 73
Jessfield Road and to pay protection fees to the
same organ with effect from date.

In compliance with the instructions, the
conductors of the various dens, some of whom had
obtained advanced information to the effect that
their permits would be withdrawn either on March 10
or 20, 1940, immediately called at 73 Jessfield Road.
They handed in their permits and were assured that
they would be permitted to continue operation under
the joint protection of the Japanese Military Police
and the members of the Special Service Corps of the
Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern & National
Salvation Army. New permits, they were informed,
may be issued to them after the formal inauguration
of Wang Ching Wei Administration.

The gambling dens in the Western District
which were scheduled to close down at the end
of February, 1940, in accordance with a
reorganization scheme, have been promised by
the Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department
that the scheme will be postponed for a time.

According to confidential information
received by gambling den conductors from persons
connected with the Amusement Supervision Department,
9/470 Yu Yuen Road, the Department will withdraw
the licences of all gambling dens in the Western
District, O.O.L., on March 10 or 20, 1940 when
the affairs pertaining to the control of the
establishments will be handed over to the Wang
Ching Wei administration. Further, in view
of the agitation against their closing down,
the new controlling organ, it is said, will permit
the gambling dens to carry on until May 31, 1940
but will increase the fees by more than 30%
and demand payment of the same in advance in a
lump sum. By this method, it is expected that
the smaller gambling dens, being unable to make
such a large payment, will be compelled to close
down.

CHINA PRESS.
FEB 29 1940

Gambling Dens
Now Given
To March 20

Reports published by THE CHINA
PRESS yesterday that the deadline
for the western district vice dens
had been extended to March 10
were again outdated yesterday, when
it was learned that it had been
again extended to March 20.
This further extension, it was
announced, would be the last, and
was granted in order to give the
gambling and opium dens suffici-
ent time to wind up their "rackets"
and to enable those of them who
so wished to establish 'businesses'
in Nantao.
According to this report, licenses
will be granted for 16 gambling dens
in Nantao, and indications that the
Chinese City on the southeastern
borders of the French Concession
would be developed into a second
Badlands were stronger than before.
Already four gambling houses, as
well as a number of narcotic dens,
are operating in Nantao. Unim-
pressive establishments so far, it is
stated that they will also develop
into extravagant casinos in time.
It will be recalled that an identical
situation arose in the western dis-
trict late in 1938, where the first
gambling houses were bleak, wood-
en structures.

C. J. J. Ch

《字林西报》。
1940年2月29日

赌场
现延至
3月20日

《字林西报》昨日刊登的报道曾称，西区罪恶场所的最后期限已延长至3月10日，但昨日获悉该期限再次延长至3月20日，故前述报道又已过时。
据宣布，此次进一步延期将是最后一次，目的是给予赌场和鸦片馆足够的时间来结束其“非法勾当”，并使其中希望者在南市建立“业务”。
据报道，南市将颁发16家赌场的执照，且迹象表明，法租界东南边界的中国城将被发展成为第二个“坏地带”（Badlands），这种可能性比以往更强。目前已有四家赌馆以及多家毒品馆在南市运营。据说，尽管目前的场所并不起眼，但它们迟早也会发展成奢华的赌场。
回想起来，1938年末西区也出现过类似的情况，那里的第一批赌场曾是简陋的木制建筑。

Gambling Forbidden
In Nantao

Authorities Will Enforce
Order in District

The wholesale closure of newly
established gambling houses in Nan-
tao, which was reported last Satur-
day, might have been due to official
action as it is reported by the "Sin
Shun Pao" that the Chinese police
in Nantao have received orders to
forbid gambling, including the "wah
wai" gambling lottery. It is stated
that many gamblers have been ar-
rested in Nantao during the past few
days.
The arrested persons will soon be
sent to the headquarters of the
Bureau of Public Safety of the new
Chinese city regime for questioning.
The chief reason for the official ac-
tion against gambling is said to be
preservation of order in the native
district where gambling prevention
regulations are said to have long been
enforced. The Chinese police are said
to be continuing to raid gambling
dens.
The situation still needs clarifica-
tion as it was previously reported
that gambling house managers in the
western district had decided to move
their business into Nantao, for other-
wise they would be driven out from
the area by the new joint special
police office in formation by the
Shanghai Municipal Council and Chi-
nese police. Following these reports,
gambling houses actually came into
existence in the native city.
These Nantao establishments are
now being suppressed by the Chi-
nese police, while the western dis-
trict gambling houses have shown no
signs of closing. Reports are current
that the establishments in "badlands"
require a much bigger police force
to close them than at first imagined.
page_data.zh:
南市禁止赌博

当局将在该区执行命令

上周六报道的南市新设赌场的大规模关闭，可能是官方行动所致，因为据《新闻报》报道，南市的华捕已接到命令，禁止包括“花会”彩票在内的赌博活动。据悉，过去几天南市已逮捕多名赌徒。
被捕人员很快将被送往新城政权公共安全局总部接受讯问。
据称，官方采取反赌博行动的主要原因是为了维持华界地区的秩序，据说该地区长期执行禁赌规定。据悉，华捕正在继续突袭赌场。
局势仍需澄清，因为此前有报道称，西区赌场经理决定将业务迁往南市，否则他们将被上海工部局和华警正在组建的联合特别警察办事处驱逐出该地区。在这些报道之后，华界确实出现了赌场。
目前，这些南市场所正受到华警的镇压，而西区赌场则没有显示出关闭的迹象。目前有传言称，关闭这些“坏地带”的场所所需的警力比最初想象的要大得多。

page_data.en:
Badlands Gambling
Houses Said Given
Respite

Promises, Threats
Bring Postponement
Of Closure Decrees

Japanese Said Allowing Continued Existence
Of Dens On Conditions; Soaring License
Price Indicates Confidence

Big Resort Opening Doors In Nantao

"It comes ferociously like a dragon but goes as
harmlessly as a worm."
The "it" here refers to the Japanese announcements
that the gambling dens in Western Shanghai would be
closed by end of the month.

INDEFINITE RESPITE
Promises of increased "cumsha" and threats of giving
a "Roman holiday" to the armed gangsters on their payroll

have won the gambling barons of
the Western Shanghai badlands an
indefinite respite.
"It comes ferociously like a
dragon but goes as harmlessly as
a worm."
The "it" here refers to the
Japanese announcements that
the gambling dens in Western
Shanghai would be closed by end
of the month.

Indefinite Respite
Promises of increased "cumsha"
and threats of giving a "Roman
holiday" to the armed gangsters
on their payroll have won the
gambling barons of the Western
Shanghai badlands an indefinite
respite.
The gambling dens, at least
those operated by the more in-
fluential racketeers, will not be
closed down at midnight tomor-
row or on March 10 as previous-
ly hinted by Japanese authorities
but will continue to flourish for
an indefinite period.

Golden Goose
The gambling den operators, ac-
cording to reliable sources, have
convinced the Japanese authori-
ties in charge of the licensing of
these vice establishment that un-
til the enforcement of the Outside
Road Agreement, there is no need
to slay the goose which have
been laying the golden eggs.
It is even suggested that the
influential gambling den opera-
tors have pulled the strings so
effectively that the negotiations
on the agreement have been
again postponed.

Increase In Pay
In order to delay the execution
of the death sentence against the
gambling dens, the operators are
also reported to have offered an
increase in their daily tributes to
the Amusement Resort Super-
viser's Office, which at the present
amount to about $1,000,000 each
month.
While these "peaceful" negotia-
tions are going on behind the cur-
tain, more drastic action is being
taken by the armed gangsters on
the payroll of the gambling dens.
They have instigated a new crime
wave in and around the badlands
to warn the authorities that the
closure of their "life lines" would
bring about a more deteriorating
state of affairs in Western Shang-
hai. It is alleged that the daring
robberies on the buses and the
numerous highway robberies dur-
ing the last two weeks in the bad-
lands were also the work of the
armed parasites.

Market Soars
Indicating a complete con-
fidence in their own prospects,
the market value of the first-class
gambling den licenses has soared
to $100,000. Offers larger than
that sum are known to have
been made by prospective buyers
but no holders of the licenses
have so far accepted them. It is
generally believed among them
that the larger dens have a bet-
ter chance to continue their
existence than the small ones.
In granting the respite to the
gambling dens, the Japanese

authorities are reported to have
imposed several new conditions,
including:

Take Precautions
1. That the gambling dens
shall take all precautions
against shoot ups, clashes and
other incidents which may
draw unnecessary and un-
pleasant publicity.
2. That as far as possible
the gambling dens should hide
their identity behind a dis-
guise as cabarets, restaurants,
hotels, theatres, or bars.
3. That the gambling dens
must avoid displaying electric
signs to attract public atten-
tion.
Unless something untoward
happens—such as orders direct
from Tokyo—there is little like-
lihood that the number of the
gambling dens in the badlands
will show any decrease at mid-
night tomorrow or March 10, the
time rumored as chosen for the
death of these vice centers.

Nantao Sector
Meanwhile, Nantao is fast be-
coming the second badlands of
Shanghai. Four smaller dens,
catering to the lower class, are
already in full swing while a fifth
one, to be known as the San
Hsing "theatre," will be opened
soon elaborately equipped and
decorated in the Hollywood class.
The new "joint" is located at
the former site of the Overseas
Bath-House, at the New North
Gate, opposite Route Montauban.
page_data.zh:
恶土赌场
据称获暂缓

承诺与威胁
致使关闭令推迟

日方据称在特定条件下允许巢穴继续存在；执照价格飙升显示其信心

大型娱乐场所将在南市开业

“来势如龙般凶猛，去时无害如虫。”
此处的“它”指的是日方宣布将于本月底关闭上海西区赌场的消息。

无限期暂缓
承诺增加“贡金”（cumsha）以及威胁要对受其雇佣的武装歹徒上演一场“罗马假日”式的屠杀，这些手段为上海西区恶土的赌博大亨们赢得了无限期的暂缓。
“来势如龙般凶猛，去时无害如虫。”
此处的“它”指的是日方宣布将于本月底关闭上海西区赌场的消息。

无限期暂缓
承诺增加“贡金”（cumsha）以及威胁要对受其雇佣的武装歹徒上演一场“罗马假日”式的屠杀，这些手段为上海西区恶土的赌博大亨们赢得了无限期的暂缓。
赌场，至少是由那些更有影响力的勒索者经营的那些，将不会像日本当局此前暗示的那样在明天午夜或3月10日被关闭，而是将在一段不确定的时期内继续繁荣。

摇钱树
据可靠消息来源称，赌场经营者已说服负责此类罪恶场所发证的日本当局，认为在《越界筑路协定》（Outside Road Agreement）执行之前，没有必要杀掉这只一直下金蛋的鹅。
甚至有建议称，有影响力的赌场经营者幕后操纵得如此有效，以至于关于该协定的谈判再次被推迟。

增加进贡
据报道，为了延缓对赌场执行“死刑”，经营者还提出增加每日向娱乐业监理处缴纳的贡金，目前这笔款项每月约为100万元。
当这些“和平”谈判在幕后进行时，受赌场雇佣的武装歹徒正在采取更激烈的行动。他们在恶土及其周边地区煽动了一波新的犯罪浪潮，以警告当局：关闭他们的“生命线”将导致上海西区的局势进一步恶化。据称，过去两周在恶土地区发生的公交车大胆抢劫案和多次公路抢劫案，也是这些武装寄生虫所为。

市场飙升
出于对自身前景的完全自信，一级赌场执照的市场价值已飙升至10万元。据悉，潜在买家提出的报价甚至高于此金额，但至今没有执照持有者接受。他们普遍认为，大型赌场比小型赌场更有机会继续存在。
据报道，日本当局在给予赌场暂缓关闭的同时，施加了几项新条件，包括：

采取预防措施
1. 赌场应采取一切预防措施，防止枪战、冲突和其他可能引起不必要且令人不快的公众关注的事件。
2. 赌场应尽可能将其身份隐藏在歌舞厅、餐馆、酒店、剧院或酒吧等伪装之下。
3. 赌场必须避免展示吸引公众注意的电气招牌。
除非发生不幸事件——例如来自东京的直接命令——否则明天午夜或3月10日（传闻中选定为这些罪恶中心灭亡的时间），恶土地区的赌场数量不太可能减少。

南市区域
与此同时，南市正迅速成为上海的第二个恶土区。四家面向下层阶级的小型赌场已经全面营业，而第五家名为三星（San Hsing）“剧院”的赌场即将开业，其设施和华丽的装饰将达到好莱坞级别。这家新的“窝点”位于新北门原海外浴室旧址，对面是蒙托邦路（Route Montauban）。

Date February 22, 1940.
Subject Gambling dens in Western District - agitation against closing down.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Further to report of this office dated 21/2/40
on gambling dens in the Western District being pro-
hibited by the Shanghai Amusement Supervision Depart-
ment, 9/470 Yu Yuen Road, O.C.L., from illuminating
their advertisement boards with effect from February
21, the Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department
rescinded the order in the afternoon of the same day
after repeated petitions made by the gambling den
owners through T.G. Lee (李秋野) otherwise known
as G. Akino, a Korean and an influential member of
the Japanese Special Service Section.

T.G. Lee presented altogether four demands to
Sasaki, Chief of the Amusement Supervision Department,
on behalf of the gambling den owners. They are:-
1. That the order instructing the gambling dens not
to illuminate their advertisement boards facing
the street be rescinded on the grounds that such
a step will seriously affect the business of the
establishments.
2. That all the gambling dens without exception be
allowed to continue operation after February 29,
1940.
3. That in case the second mentioned demand is granted,
the gambling dens will reconstruct their entrances
so as to give the appearance of theatres or
restaurants and thereby minimize criticism from
the public.

（左侧栏内容）
Comm: of Police
Sir:
I forward.
R.H. Forster

由 特别分部督察 廖仲坚 制作 经由 督察 克劳福德 转呈

继本处于1940年2月21日关于上海娱乐业监理处禁止西区赌场的报告之后，该处位于愚园路470号9弄（O.C.L.）曾下令自2月21日起不得点亮广告灯箱。然而，在同日下午，经过赌场老板通过李秋野（T.G. Lee，又名 G. Akino，朝鲜人，日本特务机关颇具影响力的成员）反复请愿后，上海娱乐业监理处撤销了该命令。

李秋野代表赌场老板向娱乐业监理处处长佐佐木（Sasaki）共提出了四项要求。它们是：-
1. 以严重影响场所生意为由，撤销禁止赌场点亮面向街道的广告灯箱的命令。
2. 允许所有赌场无一例外地在1940年2月29日后继续营业。
3. 如果上述第二项要求获得批准，赌场将重建入口，使其看起来像剧院或餐馆，从而最大限度地减少公众的批评。

MALE CHINESE SUFFERING FROM BULLET WOUNDS.

At 9p.m. 14/2/40 C.C.R. reported that a S.F.B.
Ambulance had been called to Great Western Road near
Columbia Road.

Enquiries were made at the Chinese Red Cross
Hospital, Avenue Haig, and it was learned that a male
Chinese named Zung Ching Fah (沈廷芳), 39, Ningpo,
m/master carpenter, living at lane 185/8 Tunsin Road,
had been treated for bullet wounds. He was certified
as follows and discharged:- "(1) Gunshot wound, through
and through right shoulder region. (2) Lacerated wounds
of scalp. Condition O.K.".

Zung Ching Fah stated that at about 8.45p.m.
14/2/40 while he was watching several persons gambling
at No. 20 Doong Tuh Li (同德里) TUNSIN Rd (Chinese territory),
five armed members of the S.C.G.P.B. raided the place
and ordered all not to move. The gamblers disobeyed
and in the scurry to escape from the house one of the
S.C.G.P.B. Constables fired a shot which entered Zung's
right upper arm came out on the point of the shoulder
and grazed the back of his head (He was bending at the
time). He was then taken to the S.C.P. Sub Bureau on
Great Western Road near Columbia Road, and after the
S.C.G.P.B. had called a S.F.B. ambulance he was placed
on the pathway to await its arrival.

一名身中枪伤的华籍男子。

1940年2月14日晚9时，中央捕房报告称，一辆圣约翰救伤队（S.F.B.）救护车被召往哥伦比亚路附近的大西路。

经在海格路中国红十字会医院查询，获悉一名名为沈廷芳（Zung Ching Fah），39岁，宁波人，职业木匠，住同新路185弄8号的华籍男子因枪伤接受治疗。其诊断证明及出院记录如下：“(1) 右肩区域贯通枪伤。(2) 头皮裂伤。状况良好。”

沈廷芳称，1940年2月14日晚8时45分左右，当他在同新路同德里20号（中国地界）观看数人赌博时，五名武装的上海特别市政府警察局（S.C.G.P.B.）人员突袭该处，命令所有人不得移动。赌徒们未服从命令，在慌乱逃窜过程中，一名上海特别市政府警察局警员开枪，子弹穿过沈的右上臂，从肩部穿出，并擦过其后脑（当时他正弯着腰）。随后他被带至哥伦比亚路附近大西路的上海特别市政府警察局分局，在上海特别市政府警察局呼叫圣约翰救伤队救护车后，他被安置在人行道上等待救护车到达。

Date February 13, 1940.

Subject Gambling Dens in Western District to suspend operation at the
end of February, 1940 pending reorganization by Wang Ching
Wei's Administration.
Made by D.S.I. Lino Chung Chien Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

With reference to the attached report from Bubbling
Well Station to the effect that the gambling dens in
the Western District have been instructed to cease
functioning on February 29, 1940, discreet enquiries
have confirmed the report and have elicited the
information that the step is the outcome of an agreement
reached between the Japanese Authorities and the Wang
Ching Wei Administration which is scheduled to be
inaugurated on March 15, 1940.

According to the agreement, the Shanghai Amusement
Supervision Department, 9/470 Yu Yuen Road (Japanese
sponsored), which has controlled the gambling dens in
the Western District since their formation at the end
of 1937, will hand over all affairs pertaining to the
gambling dens to Wang Ching Wei's Administration at
the end of February 1940 when a reorganization of the
establishments will take place. Although the scheme
of reorganization to be undertaken is not yet known,
it is learned from a reliable source that of the
twenty-four gambling dens in the Western District only
six to ten of the larger establishments will be permitted
to reopen in future but they will be required to furnish
between them a sum equivalent to the protection fees paid
by those dens to be closed as a result of the reorganiza-
tion.

参照静安寺捕房的附件报告，其中称西区赌场已接到指令，于1940年2月29日停止运营。经 discreet enquiries（谨慎查询）证实了该报告，并获悉此举是日本当局与定于1940年3月15日正式成立的汪精卫政府之间达成协议的结果。

根据协议，自1937年底成立以来一直控制西区赌场的上海娱乐监管部（日方资助，地址：愚园路9/470号），将于1940年2月底将所有与赌场有关的事务移交给汪精卫政府，届时将对这些场所进行重组。虽然具体的重组方案尚不清楚，但从可靠消息来源获悉，西区的二十四家赌场中，未来仅允许六至十家较大的场所重新开业，但它们需共同提供一笔相当于那些因重组而关闭的赌场所缴纳的保护费的金额。

The "Hwo-wei" lottery establishments in the Western District, O.O.L., it is reported, will be treated in a similar fashion.

Meanwhile a number of the promoters of the smaller gambling dens and "Hwo-wei" lottery organizations in the Western District are agitating against the order for the closing down of their establishments and are urging Sasaki, Chief of the Shanghai Amusement Supervision Department, 9/470 Yu Yuen Road, to maintain the "status quo." However, it is generally viewed that the agitation will be fruitless and some of the gambling den conductors are contemplating the removal of their establishments to Nantao. Up to the present, it is learned that the following premises in Nantao have been leased for the purpose of conducting gambling:-

1. No.725 Zao Chia Road, Old West Gate, Nantao.
2. No.1451, Chung Hwa Road, Nantao.
3. No.1603, Chung Hwa Road, Nantao.

The first mentioned house is leased by Kao Ah Keng (高阿根), proprietor of Dah Sung Gambling Den, situated in Sing Kong Li, Connaught Road, O.O.L., while the second and third houses have on their gates posters bearing the inscriptions, "Commandeered by Japanese Consulate-General," and "Commandeered by the Special Service Section of the Japanese Military," respectively. The actual lessees of these two houses, however, cannot be ascertained at the present.

1. 南市老西门赵家路725号。

第一处房屋由位于康纳特路新康里的达盛赌场老板高阿根（Kao Ah Keng）租赁，而第二和第三处房屋的大门上分别贴有“日本总领事馆征用”和“日本军方特务机关征用”字样的告示。然而，目前尚无法查明这两处房屋的实际承租人。
